For the direct linear-stage branch, optionally supply exact pointwise coefficient maps $A:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $B:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ satisfying $f(t,x,u)=A(t)x+B(t)u$ at every queried stage input; only this explicit representation enables that branch. Supply a deterministic derivative evaluator for the actual returned stage maps and resulting finite NLP on an open neighborhood of the queried candidate. On a locally fixed strict stopping branch of the finite stage-iteration procedure, differentiate that finite graph, including when the residual happens to be exactly zero at the queried point. Implicit differentiation as in [[thm-implicit-differentiation-forward-and-adjoint-formulas]] is permitted only when the selected returned stage map is certified to agree on that neighborhood with the exact local solution branch and its residual Jacobian is nonsingular there; an exact residual at the queried point alone does not establish this agreement. Return `derivative-failure` when no derivative of the actual returned map is available. Supply a quadrature error evaluator which returns a certified upper bound for the objective quadrature discrepancy or `unavailable`. Each supplied evaluator returns a value or failure in finite time. An optional trajectory-estimation request supplies the inputs of [[alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-controller]].
$$X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_{k<i}a_{ik}F_{j,k},\quad t_{j,i}=t_j+c_ih_j,\quad F_{j,i}=f(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j),\quad \Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_i b_iF_{j,i}.$$

**Mesh and constraints.** Check that the original mesh satisfies $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$ and that all declared constraint and quadrature times lie in $[0,T]$; if either check fails, return `mesh-domain-failure` without evaluation. If the original node count exceeds the supplied cap, return `mesh-budget-exhausted`. Insert every declared path-constraint time not already a node, unless this exceeds the node cap, in which case return `mesh-budget-exhausted`. Tie each inserted subcell's control to its original containing cell, so the parameterization is unchanged. On the resulting mesh, check all stage times $t_j+c_i h_j$ lie in $[0,T]$ before querying $f$ or $L$; an invalid time returns `mesh-domain-failure` with no evaluation. Each tableau stage and its quadrature contribution use the control $u_j$ of that cell, as in the stage equations below. At a declared path- or endpoint-constraint time that is a mesh node before $T$, use the right-hand original-cell value from the half-open representative in [[def-ctrl1-control-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-parameterization]]; at $T$, use the last original-cell control value unless a separate endpoint-control variable is supplied. Use the same convention at separately declared non-stage quadrature times. An endpoint constraint is evaluated at its declared endpoint. This is finite sampling and does not assert continuous-path feasibility.

**Stage evaluation.** On each cell write $h_j=t_{j+1}-t_j$ and $u_j$ for its tied constant control. Before forming any stages, check $X_{j,0}\in\Omega_x$ and $u_j\in\Omega_u$; a failed check returns `stage-domain-failure` with the cell and no objective candidate. For an explicit tableau, form the stages recursively by the displayed equations. Before each query of $f$ or $L$, check that the time is in $[0,T]$, the state lies in $\Omega_x$, and the control lies in $\Omega_u$; a failed membership check returns `stage-domain-failure`, and an unavailable function value returns `stage-evaluation-failure` with the cell and stage index. Apply the same checks to every declared path-constraint evaluation.

For an implicit tableau, do not leave the collocation stages as outer NLP decision variables. Form the coupled slope residual
$$R_j(K;X_{j,0},u_j)_i=K_i-f\!\left(t_j+c_ih_j,X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_k a_{ik}K_k,u_j\right),\quad i=1,\ldots,s.$$
With the stage times fixed and already checked in $[0,T]$, its open evaluation domain consists of stage vectors for which every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and the cell control lies in $\Omega_u$; require $R_j$ to be $C^1$ on this domain. A compact tube used for bounds does not replace this open evaluation domain. If exact coefficient maps $A,B$ were supplied and satisfy $f(t,x,u)=A(t)x+B(t)u$ at every queried stage input, form the finite matrix $M_j$ with blocks $(M_j)_{ik}=\delta_{ik}I-h_ja_{ik}A(t_{j,i})$ and right-hand side $r_i=A(t_{j,i})X_{j,0}+B(t_{j,i})u_j$. Use exact Gaussian elimination on the stored sample coefficients: scan columns left to right, pivot on the first nonzero entry at or below the current row, swap, eliminate below, and back-substitute. If no pivot is available, return `singular-stage-matrix`; otherwise form every induced stage state and check every stage time-state-control input belongs to the smooth-data tube. A failed domain check returns `stage-domain-failure` with the failing cell and stage index, the partial result record, and no objective candidate. Before calling Newton, check that the entire seed $K^{(0)}$ belongs to the declared open domain of $R_j$, equivalently that every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and every required control lies in $\Omega_u$. Otherwise call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $R_j$ with that open evaluation domain, tolerance $\tau_s$ and cap $M_s$. Record its iterate, residual vector, and exact status for each cell. Only `root` supplies a stage candidate; it means $\|R_j\|_2\le\tau_s$, not an exact root unless $\tau_s=0$. Any other status returns the partial result record with `nlp_status=stage-solve-failure`, the failing cell, and no objective candidate. Include a model that can reevaluate these quantities at a later solver candidate. Return separate `nlp_status`, per-cell `implicit_stage_status`, optional `ivp_status`, `quadrature_status`, `mesh_status`, and `budget_status` fields. A quadrature bound at most $\tau_q$ is `bound-met`; a larger bound is `bound-not-met`; an unavailable bound is `unavailable`. The build-stage budget field is `not-run`; the solver dispatcher fills its final value. A failed derivative evaluation leaves KKT residuals unavailable with its exact status. An unevaluated optional IVP estimate is `not-requested`; if requested, report the adaptive controller's exact finite status, not an error certificate.

This direct transcription samples pointwise data; an $L^\infty$ equivalence class without a chosen representative and sampling rule is not stage-evaluable. For a single-shooting reduced objective represented as the finite state-step graph of [[def-parameterized-finite-state-step-objective]], its exact real-arithmetic reduced gradient is given by [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]. Agreement with the continuous ODE adjoint gradient is only conditional on the weighted discrete-gradient representation and the separate state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint, and quadrature estimates in [[thm-discrete-continuous-gradient-error-order-p]]. The optional adaptive RK estimate is separate from the fixed NLP and its embedded difference is not a certified global error bound. If all construction, stage, sample-domain and objective checks succeed, return `nlp_status=constructed` for a solver-ready NLP, or `nlp_status=not-smooth-nlp` for a finite set-constrained model without a smooth control representation; set `mesh_status=valid` and retain `budget_status=not-run`. $$R_j(K;X_{j,0},u_j)_i=K_i-f\!\left(t_j+c_ih_j,X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_k a_{ik}K_k,u_j\right),\quad i=1,\ldots,s.$$
With the stage times fixed and already checked in $[0,T]$, its open evaluation domain consists of stage vectors for which every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and the cell control lies in $\Omega_u$; require $R_j$ to be $C^1$ on this domain. A compact tube used for bounds does not replace this open evaluation domain. If exact coefficient maps $A,B$ were supplied and satisfy $f(t,x,u)=A(t)x+B(t)u$ at every queried stage input, form the finite matrix $M_j$ with blocks $(M_j)_{ik}=\delta_{ik}I-h_ja_{ik}A(t_{j,i})$ and right-hand side $r_i=A(t_{j,i})X_{j,0}+B(t_{j,i})u_j$. Use exact Gaussian elimination on the stored sample coefficients: scan columns left to right, pivot on the first nonzero entry at or below the current row, swap, eliminate below, and back-substitute. If no pivot is available, return `singular-stage-matrix`; otherwise form every induced stage state and check every stage time-state-control input belongs to the smooth-data tube. A failed domain check returns `stage-domain-failure` with the failing cell and stage index, the partial result record, and no objective candidate. If all checks pass, the exact solution of $M_jK=r$ is the stage vector and the nonlinear-solve status is `exact-linear-stage-solve`. In all other smooth cases, form the deterministic initial guess $K_i^{(0)}=f(t_j,X_{j,0},u_j)$ after checking that this query is defined. Before calling Newton, check that the entire seed $K^{(0)}$ belongs to the declared open domain of $R_j$, equivalently that every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and every required control lies in $\Omega_u$. If this check fails, return `stage-domain-failure` with the failing cell and stage index, the partial result record, and no objective candidate. Otherwise call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $R_j$ with that open evaluation domain, tolerance $\tau_s$ and cap $M_s$. Record its iterate, residual vector, and exact status for each cell. Only `root` supplies a stage candidate; it means $\|R_j\|_2\le\tau_s$, not an exact root unless $\tau_s=0$. Any other status returns the partial result record with `nlp_status=stage-solve-failure`, the failing cell, and no objective candidate. On a returned stage vector use $X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_k a_{ik}K_k$ and $\Phi_j=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_i b_iK_i$. A singular stage Jacobian or failed stage query is reported, not interpreted as lack of an exact solution.

**Transcription modes.** In single shooting, the decision variables are the original-cell controls; set $X_{0,0}=x_0$ and recursively compute $X_{j+1,0}=\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$. In multiple shooting, the decision variables are node states and controls; fix $X_{0,0}=x_0$, define defects $d_j=X_{j+1,0}-\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$, and impose $d_j=0$ for every $j=0,\ldots,N-1$. In collocation mode, use the same node/control variables, fixed initial state, continuity equalities $d_j=0$, and solved internal stage states; the collocation equations are solved internally by the implicit-stage procedure above. Explicit stages are likewise internal deterministic evaluations. After every interval map in every mode, check $\Phi_j\in\Omega_x$ before using it as a later start or evaluating a path constraint, terminal cost, or endpoint constraint; otherwise return `stage-domain-failure` with no objective candidate. Independently of the computed endpoints and defect residuals, check $X_{N,0}\in\Omega_x$ before evaluating $\phi(X_{N,0})$ or any terminal constraint; in multiple shooting and collocation this node is an independent decision variable even when $\Phi_{N-1}\in\Omega_x$. Before any endpoint-constraint query, also check every actual state and control argument, including a separately supplied endpoint-control variable, belongs to that function's declared domain. Any failed membership check returns `stage-domain-failure` with no objective candidate. In every mode the finite feasible set includes $u_j\in U_c$ for each original cell. The finite objective is $\sum_j h_j\sum_i b_iL(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j)+\phi(X_{N,0})$, and the finite constraints are exactly the fixed initial-state condition, the continuity equalities $d_j=0$ for every cell in multiple-shooting and collocation modes, the declared node/time constraints, the represented control constraints, and endpoint constraints. Single shooting enforces its initial state and dynamics by substitution. In multiple shooting and collocation, include every component of every $d_j$ in the equality residual $h$ and its derivatives in $Dh$ for the NLP and KKT residuals. A candidate may have nonzero defects: these are constraint residuals, not a stage-construction failure. The equalities use the actual returned deterministic interval maps; the internal stage tolerance $\tau_s$ does not relax the continuity equalities or assert that an approximate implicit stage vector is an exact Runge--Kutta stage solution. If $U_c$ is available only as a compact set-membership constraint and has no finite smooth representation, return the finite set-constrained model with `nlp_status=not-smooth-nlp`; the dispatcher must not treat it as an SQP-ready NLP. A QP solver route additionally requires the sampled control constraints to be affine.

**Output.** Evaluate the supplied initial candidate and return a record containing its ordered decision variables, defect residuals, per-cell implicit-stage residuals, path/endpoint constraint residuals, KKT residuals, and objective value, when available. For equality residual $h$, inequality residual $g\le0$, and multiplier pair $(\nu,\lambda)$, report $r_p=(h,[g]_+)$, $r_d=\nabla J_N+Dh^T\nu+Dg^T\lambda$, $r_\lambda=[-\lambda]_+$, and $r_c=\lambda\odot g$. Include a model that can reevaluate these quantities at a later solver candidate. Return separate `nlp_status`, per-cell `implicit_stage_status`, optional `ivp_status`, `quadrature_status`, `mesh_status`, and `budget_status` fields. A quadrature bound at most $\tau_q$ is `bound-met`; a larger bound is `bound-not-met`; an unavailable bound is `unavailable`. The build-stage budget field is `not-run`; the solver dispatcher fills its final value. A failed derivative evaluation leaves KKT residuals unavailable with its exact status. An unevaluated optional IVP estimate is `not-requested`; if requested, report the adaptive controller's exact finite status, not an error certificate.

This direct transcription samples pointwise data; an $L^\infty$ equivalence class without a chosen representative and sampling rule is not stage-evaluable. For a single-shooting reduced objective represented as the finite state-step graph of [[def-parameterized-finite-state-step-objective]], its exact real-arithmetic reduced gradient is given by [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]. Agreement with the continuous ODE adjoint gradient is only conditional on the weighted discrete-gradient representation and the separate state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint, and quadrature estimates in [[thm-discrete-continuous-gradient-error-order-p]]. The optional adaptive RK estimate is separate from the fixed NLP and its embedded difference is not a certified global error bound. If all construction, stage, sample-domain and objective checks succeed, return `nlp_status=constructed` for a solver-ready NLP, or `nlp_status=not-smooth-nlp` for a finite set-constrained model without a smooth control representation; set `mesh_status=valid` and retain `budget_status=not-run`. The algorithm makes no continuous-path feasibility, convergence-rate, global-optimality, or unconditioned discrete-adjoint accuracy claim.
